fix: hide rebase all before first paint

The Bots page rendered the Rebase all block visible and hid it only once the first snapshot reached `updateRebaseAll`, so an empty button could flash on load.

- The block now starts with the `hidden` attribute. `updateRebaseAll` already shows it when something is out of date or a run is in progress.
- New e2e check records the block's `hidden` state the moment it is inserted (red before, green after), plus an axe scan in that state.
- Two commits: the fix, then a type fix for the test probe (`Element.hidden` is `boolean | string` in the DOM lib, which the pre-push `tsc` caught). Squash merge folds them.

Closes #2945

fix(loadtest): name a malformed tokens line or steps entry, and clear Sonar's Groovy findings

## Why

The SonarCloud quality gate on main has been red since the analysis of ade4ca8 on 2026-10-27, when SonarCloud changed its Groovy profile. `tests/load/jmeter/pick.groovy`, the script the load test plan runs before each request, got two groovydre:S8361 bugs, which put the new-code reliability rating at D, and twelve code smells: S134 (nesting deeper than three levels), S8306 (an if body without braces), and S1192 (the literal `loadtest.tokens` three times).

The two bugs are real. The script indexed the fields of a tokens file line without checking how many there were, so a line with fewer than three fields failed the script with `java.lang.ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 2 out of bounds for length 2`, which names neither the file nor the line. `loadkit tokens` writes the file through a rename and never writes such a line, so only a file written by hand or by another tool reaches it. A `steps` or `hotSteps` entry without a colon, such as `1000`, failed the same way with `Index 1 out of bounds for length 1`; Sonar did not flag that one.

## What

- A tokens file line with fewer than three fields fails with `line <n> of <file> is not user,hot,token`. A `steps` or `hotSteps` entry that is not `rate:seconds` fails with `steps entry '1000' is not rate:seconds`, naming its property; an entry with three parts, of which the script read the first two, is refused too. As before, a failing script stops the thread, since the plan's `op` stays `STOP` until the script sets it.
- The shared schedule and the tokens file are read in methods of their own (`schedule`, `readSteps`, `tokenState`, `readTokens`), which keeps the nesting at three levels. Every if body has braces, and the property that holds the tokens is the constant `TOKEN_STATE`. For a well-formed tokens file and well-formed steps the script sets the same variables as before.

## How to verify

The repository has no Groovy test harness. I ran the old and the new script through a local harness that does what the JMeter JSR223 PreProcessor does: compile once with Groovy 3.0.20, the version JMeter 5.6.3 bundles, and evaluate per request with `ctx`, `vars`, and `props` bound. Both scripts pass the same checks of the well-formed path: arrival counts and the rate-0 gap of the schedule, hot users taken in turn, background users drawn from the users that are not hot, the operation mix, wait and lag, the tokens file read again only after five seconds and only when it changed, with the hot users' counter kept, and eight threads sharing one schedule. The old script fails the four checks of the new errors (a two-field and a one-field tokens line, a steps entry without a colon, a hotSteps entry with three parts) with `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException` or no error. Mutants of the new script that drop the counter on a reread, reread on every request, or stop skipping blank lines fail the harness.

The `Load test` workflow runs the kit end to end on kind for this pull request. Whether SonarCloud clears the fourteen findings shows on this pull request's analysis.

## Scope

The eighteen go:S3776 findings (cognitive complexity) open on main are not part of this change. They do not fail the gate: the new-code maintainability rating is A. Neither is a harness in the repository that runs the script outside JMeter: the repository has no Groovy toolchain, and CI would need one.

benchmarks.task_description:
fix: hide Rebase all when nothing is out of date

The Bots page kept a disabled Rebase all button and a line saying nothing was out of date. With no listed pull request behind there is nothing to offer, so the button and its line now go away.

- Shown while any listed row is out of date, or while a run is in progress (a pure decision, `showRebaseAll`, unit tested).
- Hidden with the `hidden` attribute, so it leaves the accessibility tree and tab order.
- If the button had focus when it goes, focus moves to the All quick filter.
- The status live region sits outside the hidden block, so a finished run is still announced.
- Docs updated.

No other page has a page-level rebase control. Pull requests, Issues, Insights and Releases only have per-row actions.

One note on the mid-run case: the board holds snapshots while a row action is in flight, so rows can't stop being behind mid-run in a browser. The unit test covers the decision, and the e2e checks the progress label stays through a run, then the button goes after the next snapshot.

Closes #2939

Fix database count for latest incremental backup metrics.

- Fix pgbackrest_backup_last_databases so incr uses the differential backup's database count when incr and diff select the same backup.
- Allow processSpecificBackupData to populate multiple backup types from one pgBackRest query while preserving parallel collection.
- Reuse the full backup's count only when incr selects the full backup.
- Add regression coverage for shared and distinct backup selections and check that each selected backup is queried once.
